ledger.x: 320: Chandragupta I is crowned and takes the title Maharajadhiraja.

c. 347: Samudragupta uproots the kings of Aryavarta. Allahabad Pillar: the Gupta Empire page says it 'asserts that Samudragupta uprooted 8 kings of Āryāvarta'; the Samudragupta page names them (Achyuta of Ahichchhatra, Nagasena of Padmavati, Ganapati-naga, Rudradeva, Matila, Nagadatta, Chandravarman, Balavarman, and…

c. 347: the Gupta shape takes the northern strip of the Western Satraps. The Samudragupta page lists the 'Shaka-Murundas' among foreign powers ('possibly Western Kshatrapas') and says 'Samudragupta may therefore have ousted Sridharavarman in his campaigns to the West' (Eran inscription). Cliopatria's Western Satraps…

c. 347: the rest of Samudragupta's sphere is added: the eastern kingdoms (Bengal, Bangladesh), the Odisha, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh forest kings, the Andhra coast and the hill country. Allahabad Pillar: 'Samudragupta reduced all the kings of the forest region (atavika) to subservience'; the frontier kingdoms are…
ledger.cp: Allahabad Pillar kings (frontier, forest and southern)

ledger.x: c. 347: the Kushan land of the Punjab and the north-west passes to the Gupta sphere. Kushan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Then in the mid-4th century they were subjugated by the Gupta Empire under Samudragupta' and 'They probably were vassals of the Gupta Empire'; the Samudragupta page (Eraly): 'the Kushans still…

c. 347: the Yaudheyas become Samudragupta's tributaries. Samudragupta page: the Yaudheyas ruled between the Sutlej and Yamuna after the Kushans and 'seem to have become Samudragupta's tributaries'; Yaudheya page: 'the payment of all tributes', submitting without armed resistance. Cliopatria keeps a separate Yaudheya…

c. 347: the republics and foreign powers of the Allahabad Pillar pay tribute rather than being ruled. Samudragupta page: the Malavas, Arjunayanas, Madrakas (between the Ravi and Chenab rivers), Abhiras and others; Kunal Chakrabarti argues 'the Punjab and Rajasthan republics only paid him tribute'; Eraly reads that…
ledger.cp: Allahabad Pillar tributary republics and foreign powers

ledger.x: c. 353: the Gupta shape takes the eastern edge of the Vakataka shape (Chhattisgarh and Odisha). Samudragupta page: Mahendra of Kosala and Vyaghraraja of Mahakantara were captured and released; Rudradeva, possibly a Western Kshatrapa or a Vakataka king (identity disputed), is among the Aryavarta kings. Cliopatria's…

c. 353: the Gupta shape takes 116 cells of the Pallava shape on the Andhra coast. Samudragupta page: the Samudragupta page names Vishnugopa of Kanchi (the Gupta Empire page: 'the Pallava regent of Kanchi') and the kings of Pishtapura, Kottura, Vengi (Hastivarman), Palakka (Ugrasena, possibly a Pallava viceroyalty) and…

c. 353: Kamarupa leaves the Gupta shape. Cliopatria starts its Kamarupa row in 353 and takes 91 cells from the Gupta shape; the Samudragupta page lists 'Kamarupa' and 'Davaka' among the frontier kingdoms that paid tribute, so the detachment is a drawing choice, not a page event.

c. 378: the Yaudheyas cease to be a separate tributary. Cliopatria ends the Yaudheya shape in 377 and adds exactly its 840 cells to the Gupta shape in 378. Gupta infobox predecessors include 'Yaudheya'; the Yaudheya page: 'succeeded by the Gupta Empire' and 'This particular period marked the gradual disintegration of…

c. 378: Chandragupta II's Gupta absorbs the Yaudheya republic. The 378 Gupta shape is the 358 shape plus Cliopatria's Yaudheya 377, cell for cell. Year bridged from Cliopatria; the page only names the Yaudheyas as a predecessor.

c. 380: the republics and foreign powers west of the Ganges are drawn as direct Gupta land. Chandragupta II page: his 'directly controlled territory stretched from the Oxus River in the west' to Bengal; infobox coronation c. 380. The end date is the researcher's bridge; the page does not say when tribute became rule.…
ledger.cp: Allahabad Pillar tributary republics and foreign powers

ledger.x: c. 383: a small addition on the Chhattisgarh/Odisha edge (103 cells). No page opened mentions it; recorded because Cliopatria's shape grows on 383.

c. 390: the Vakataka kingdom under Prabhavatigupta's regency. Prabhavatigupta page (opened 2026-10-19): 'she effectively ruled the Vakataka Empire as regent from about 390 to 410' (infobox 'Regency: c. 390 - 410 CE'); 'Gupta influence over the Vakatakas reached its peak'; the realm was 'practically a part of the Gupta…

c. 397: Chandragupta II's war on the Western Kshatrapas begins. Chandragupta II page: the victory 'can be tentatively dated to sometime between 397 and 409'; Rudrasimha III's last coins are Shaka year 310 or 319 'that is 388 or 397'; the Gupta Empire page says Rudrasimha III 'was defeated by 395'. The Udayagiri cave…
409: the war on the Western Kshatrapas ends.
409: Chandragupta II annexes the Western Kshatrapa kingdom.

c. 410: the Vakataka regency ends. Prabhavatigupta page: the regency ran 'from about 390 to 410'; her younger son Damodarasena (Pravarasena II) succeeded 'around 410' (the page puts Pravarasena II at c. 420-455 elsewhere, the Vakataka dynasty page at c. 400-415). The Vakataka dynasty page puts the regency at 385-405…

c. 445: Narendrasena drives the Guptas and Nalas out of the Vakataka capital. 'Around 445 CE, during the final years of Kumaragupta I's reign' he 'reclaimed his former capital by driving out the combined forces of the Guptas and Nalas'; his inscriptions claim the allegiance of Kosala, Mekala and Malava. Zone: the…

c. 451: Gupta land in Malwa, Mekala and Kosala passes to the Vakataka shape. Cliopatria's Vakataka shape gains 1,019 cells of Gupta land on 451. Narendrasena page (reign c. 455-480): the rulers of Kosala, Mekala and Malava acknowledged his authority, 'many historians' see this as exaggeration. The 451 year is…
455: the capital moves from Pataliputra to Ayodhya.

c. 461: Skandagupta recovers Malwa. Narendrasena page: 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta'; Skandagupta page: a 'c. 460-461 inscription refers to the "tranquil reign of Skandagupta, the lord of hundred kings"' and the Junagadh inscription of 457-458 shows his governor Parnadatta…

c. 461: Malwa returns to the Gupta. 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta' (Narendrasena page). The Mekala and Kosala part (Chhattisgarh) stays Vakataka. Year bridged.

c. 476: Gujarat and Saurashtra leave the Gupta shape for the Maitrakas. Maitraka dynasty page (opened 2026-10-19): the dynasty 'was founded by Senapati (general) Bhatarka', a military governor of Saurashtra under the Guptas, who 'established himself as the independent around 475 CE' (infobox 'Founded: 475'); 'During…

c. 490: the north-west goes to the Alchon Huns. Cliopatria draws the Alchon land in its White Huns row (white-huns /ledger/7 takes the Indian part of its 490 shape from alchon-huns), and its Gupta shape loses 3,303 cells to it (Rajasthan, the Punjab, Sind, Haryana). Gupta Empire page: in the late 490s the Alchon Huns…

c. 490: Malwa passes to the Vakataka shape. Harishena page (r. c. 480-510): the minister Varahadeva's Ajanta inscription describes the king's influence over Avanti among other countries; the Vakataka page: 'he conquered Avanti (Malwa)'. Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 490 lacks the Malwa cells that the Vakataka 490 shape…

c. 490: the far east and south-east edges leave the Gupta shape (about 700 cells: east Bangladesh, Tripura, Chhattisgarh, the Andhra edge, part of Odisha) to no named state. No page opened explains it; Budhagupta's viceroys at Damodarpur (Bengal) are on the Budhagupta page without a date.
496: the First Hunnic War begins on the Gupta frontier.
515: the First Hunnic War ends (the page's span 496-515).
520: the Second Hunnic War begins and Mihirakula occupies north India.
528: the Huns are driven out.
554: the Gupta Empire ends.

wars.name: Samudragupta's northern campaigns (Aryavarta)
wars.outcome: Eight kings of Aryavarta uprooted (Allahabad Pillar); their lands join the Gupta shape in the 347 jump.

wars.name: Samudragupta's southern campaign (Dakshinapatha)
wars.outcome: Twelve kings of Dakshinapatha defeated, listed as captured and released (Allahabad Pillar); no annexation and no border move on the page.

wars.name: Chandragupta II's war on the Western Kshatrapas
wars.outcome: Gupta victory; Malwa and the Kshatrapa kingdom annexed, silver coins struck, coins of 409 resemble the Kshatrapa issues.

wars.name: Narendrasena's war with the Guptas and Nalas
Skandagupta's war with the Hunas
wars.outcome: Skandagupta 'repulsed an invasion by the Indo-Hephthalites'; the Bhitari inscription describes his victory; 'The date of the Huna invasion is not certain.'

wars.name: Alchon Hun invasions of the Gupta Empire (First and Second Hunnic Wars)
wars.outcome: The Alchon Huns under Toramana and Mihirakula fight the Guptas in the First Hunnic War (496-515: Kausambi sacked 497-500, the battle of Eran 510, Toramana beaten by Prakashadharma in 515) and Mihirakula occupies north India in the Second (520 to c.
